sections.overview: This small geometrid moth belongs to genus Chiasmia and the tribe Macariini.
sections.identification: Its pale wings have a dark lattice pattern, and adults span about 20–25 mm.
sections.habitat: It occurs in dry and wet meadows, forest edges and scrub with legumes.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed on clovers and alfalfa, linking breeding to Fabaceae rather than wetland herbs.
sections.behavior: Adults are active by day and also come to artificial lights.
sections.reproduction: It usually has two generations between late April and October and overwinters as a pupa underground.
sections.ecology: Unlike the wetland geometrid Chariaspilates formosaria, this species belongs to tribe Macariini, not Gnophini.
sections.conservation: It is Least Concern in the 2023 Flemish regional assessment, not a global evaluation.
